'''Roland Lvovich Dobrushin''' ({{langx|ru|Рола́нд Льво́вич Добру́шин}}) (July 20, 1929 – November 12, 1995) was a [[mathematician]] who made important contributions to [[probability theory]],{{sfn|Ibragimov|1997}}  [[mathematical physics]],{{sfn|Minlos|1997}} and [[information theory]].{{sfn|Prelov|1997}}

==Life and work==

Dobrushin received his Ph.D. at [[Moscow State University]] under the supervision of [[Andrey Kolmogorov]].

In [[statistical mechanics]], he introduced (simultaneously with Lanford and Ruelle) the [[Dobrushin–Lanford–Ruelle equations|DLR equations]] for the [[Gibbs measure]]. Together with Kotecký and Shlosman, he studied the formation of droplets in [[Ising model|Ising-type models]], providing mathematical justification of the [[Wulff construction]].{{sfn|Jaffe|Lebowitz|Sinai|1997}}

He was a foreign member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], [[Academia Europæa]] and [[United States National Academy of Sciences|US National Academy of Sciences]].

The Dobrushin prize was established in his honour.<ref>{{cite journal|mr=2489468|title=The International Dobrushin Prize|journal=Probl. Inf. Transm.|volume=44|year=2008|issue=4|pages=395–398|doi=10.1134/s0032946008040108|s2cid=21149495}}</ref>
